title: Effective Does Not Mean Useful: Conditional Functional Substitutability for Redundancy and Scaling in Transformers
abstract: arXiv:2609.39259v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Modern neural networks scale predictably, yet the mechanisms behind these regularities remain unclear. Neural redundancy is typically characterized by component importance or representational similarity, both indirect proxies. We view redundancy as an input-conditioned, dynamic relation: intermediate computational states are functionally redundant when they induce similar downstream responses. We introduce Conditional Functional Substitutability (CFS) to directly characterize such functional substitution. CFS exposes functional relations and reduction potential missed by conventional importance- and similarity-based measures. Across modalities and Transformer families, CFS reveals systematic functional reorganization with scale. translated_title: 有效并不意味着有用：面向Transformer冗余性与规模化的条件函数可替代性
translated_abstract: 现代神经网络的可扩展性具有可预测性，但这些规律背后的机制仍不清楚。神经冗余性通常通过组件重要性或表征相似性来刻画，而这两者都是间接的代理指标。我们将冗余性视为一种依赖输入的动态关系：当中间计算状态引发相似的下游响应时，它们在功能上是冗余的。我们提出条件函数可替代性来直接刻画这种功能替代。CFS揭示了传统基于重要性和相似性的度量所遗漏的功能关系与约减潜力。跨模态和Transformer家族的实验表明，CFS揭示了随规模变化而出现的系统性功能重组。受控规模扩展实验进一步表明，性能提升并不必然伴随可替代性的增长，而具有更独立功能结构的固定容量模型表现更好，为功能……
tldr: 该论文提出条件函数可替代性（CFS）框架，将神经冗余性刻画为依赖输入的动态功能替代关系，发现性能提升与可替代性增长并不同步，且具有更独立功能结构的固定容量模型表现更好。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes Conditional Functional Substitutability (CFS), a framework that characterizes neural redundancy as an input-conditioned dynamic functional substitution relation, revealing that performance gains need not track substitutability growth and that fixed-capacity models with more independent functional structure perform better.
